accuracy.evidence: Body-part names and places match the topic evidence (head, shoulders, knees, toes, elbows, tummy) and the EYFS Development Matters guidance for 2 to 3 year olds. Elbow and knee are correctly the bends of arm and leg, toes are on feet, and every job pairing is literal and true (legs walk, hands clap, mouth eats, arms hug). The song order is the standard Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes lyric.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real toddler mix-ups: elbow versus knee (the bend step and challenge both name the other bend), toes versus fingers, whole leg versus foot, and losing top-to-bottom order in the song ('You did head. Next comes shoulders'). Wrong taps on Kit name the part that was tapped, then say where the asked part really is.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is a drawn, poseable child figure: taps are resolved to body zones, the hand and foot are dragged to fold the arm at the elbow and the leg at the knee, and Kit is assembled by dragging head, arms and legs to top, sides and bottom. Unlike the five-senses lab (objects matched to sense organs) it is about body map and joints, and it passed the 30% shingle gate.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step builds the body map: find four parts across the top, middle and bottom; tap the song parts in order going down; discover that limbs fold only at the elbow and knee by dragging; link parts to jobs; then show the whole map by building Kit. The text after each task names what was just found, so the child does first and hears the word after.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with a tempting wrong answer: 'What comes after shoulders? Toes' (toddlers skip knees), 'Where does your leg bend? It does not bend', and 'Where do the legs go? At the top'. Each is then settled by the action in that step, and the done message names the child's own choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve distinct wrong-answer m= messages: eating is the mouth, clapping is the hands, feet are at the bottom, the knee is the leg bend not the arm bend, nose comes later in the song, feet stamp rather than clap, fingers are on hands and toes on feet, so each wrong pick names the specific slip.

readability.evidence: Kid text FK -1.2 (limit 5.0 for family) with one idea per short sentence and touch prompts a grown-up can read aloud. Adult text FK 8.9 (limit 10.0). Canvas prompts are three to five words, wrap inside the right-hand column on a 360 px screen, and part buttons use the single body word.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler regex and the 12% duplication gate. Each kid paragraph covers one of place, song, bends or jobs; the adult text covers the goal, how toddlers learn the words, the named mix-ups, and the lab; the family tip is one concrete game (Touch Your) plus the song.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360x640 Android screenshots in light and dark and the phone sweep: the figure is moved left on narrow screens so prompts sit in their own column, text wraps instead of clipping (fixed after the first pass showed 'What helps you walk?' cut off), part buttons are 56 px young-size, and the build step uses pick-then-place buttons so no more than six buttons show.

accessibility.evidence: axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 in the walkthrough. Every canvas tap or drag has a labelled button (part names, Bend the elbow, Bend the knee, pick then Top, Sides or Bottom), and the canvas aria-label reads the current prompt and progress such as 'Elbow bent. Knee straight.'
